newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor CEO says beating 1996 will be hard.
newsitem.headline: Suncor CEO says beating 1996 will be hard.

text.p: Suncor Inc president and chief executive Richard George said on Thursday it will be a challenge for the company to beat its 1996 performance in 1997.

"Crude prices may not match the high levels of last year, downstream margins may remain low and we will have a one-month maintenance shutdown at our oil sands plant in the second quarter," George said in a statement.
"However, everyone at Suncor will be doing their best to deliver improved results," he added.
Suncor earned C$187 million, or C$3.42 per share, in 1996 versus C$151 million, or C$2.76 per share, the year before. Revenues were C$2.1 billion as compared with C$1.9 billion in sales in 1995.

"We had great operating and financial performance for the fourth year in a row. At the same time, we began a period of capital investment for future growth, with over C$700 million in capital projects planned for 1997," George said.
Suncor said the significant increase in earnings was primarily due to higher commodity prices and higher production at its upstream operations.

"The benefit of higher commodity prices was partially offset by crude oil and natural gas hedging, which reduced Suncor's average selling price by approximately C$2.40 per barrel of oil equivalent," Suncor said.
"Earnings were positively influenced by C$10 million in non-operational gains from asset sales," it added.
